task: Two implementations (arms) of the same change were evaluated with an identical fixed battery and single-arm reviews. Score each arm on each preregistered metric by copying the frozen value; mark unknown when the value is null. Do not rank arms or compute aggregates; closure is computed separately.

metrics.name: defect_weight
metrics.definition: 10 x confirmed high + 3 x confirmed medium + 1 x confirmed low defects; a defect is confirmed when an independent source-reading refuter failed to refute it

metrics.name: battery_pass_rate
metrics.definition: passed / applicable checks of one fixed battery run identically on each arm

metrics.name: requirements_met_rate
metrics.definition: (met + 0.5 x partial) / applicable over one shared requirement list, graded by a reviewer who saw only that arm

metrics.name: own_suite_pass
metrics.definition: 1 when every acceptance command of the arm exits 0 at its head, else 0

confirmed_defects.summary: The regression tests do not actually enforce the failure-path behavior the decision record claims they guard, since removing a cancellation-guard condition from one results-upload step, or adding an always-run condition to another artifact step, would still pass the tests.

A configuration file's header states it applies only to one dependency ecosystem and that no version-update entry belongs there, but the file now contains an entry for a second ecosystem, and several docs still claim the automated dependency updater manages only the first ecosystem's references.

A section of the decision record claims only one job holds a sensitive write permission and rejects a proposed alternative on the grounds that it would scan twice, yet the design that was actually chosen already performs two scans on non-pull-request events, contradicting the stated rejection reason.

The decision record omits required elements for several described changes: one section lacks any evidence or measured result and any alternatives considered, and two other sections lack any alternatives-considered discussion at all.

confirmed_defects.summary: When a static-analysis scanner crashes, its job still produces an empty results file and lets the downstream upload job run, which violates the stated requirement that a crash must never lead to uploading an empty or invalid results file, and reintroduces a previously fixed duplicate-failure condition.
One analysis job fails when it merely detects findings, contradicting the stated requirement that only a tool crash, not the findings themselves, should fail the job.

The decision record claims an upload step now runs only when the preceding analysis job actually produced a results file, but this holds only for failures occurring before one particular step in that job, not for failures happening after it.
Documentation still describes a dependency vulnerability-scanning job as report-only and non-blocking, even though this change made it a gating, blocking check.

A previously recorded open gap, stating that a hosted vulnerability-scanning job has no recorded run identifier, was left unamended even though this change cites a specific hosted run identifier as its comparison baseline.
The baseline and measured source tree referenced in the decision record do not match the actual checkout this change ships with, making the recorded scan result and its expected-failure note stale.

An upload step also executes after a scanner error, so it can attempt to upload a missing or partial results file and introduce a second failure, because its run condition does not distinguish a findings-only exit from an actual tool error.

A test validating suppression entries in a vulnerability-ignore configuration checks only one type of suppression entry, so other suppression settings in that same file could silently weaken a severity gate without any justification or review date being required.
